name: Neo4j, Inc. (formerly Neo Technology)
origin_detail: Started in Sweden in 2007 by Emil Eifrem, Johan Svensson and Peter Neubauer (Eifrem sketched the idea in 2000). Moved to Silicon Valley in 2011 to raise venture funding; HQ San Mateo, California, with engineering in Sweden.
openness_notes: Community Edition GPLv3; Enterprise Edition was dual-licensed under open-source terms (parts AGPLv3 with the Commons Clause added) and commercial licences. A 2018-11-15 Neo4j blog announced an open-core model, and Enterprise (and the newer Infinigraph edition) is now closed-source commercial. Community stays GPLv3: level 2.

license_history.license: GPLv3 (Community); Enterprise under open-source (AGPLv3) terms plus commercial licences
Enterprise Edition closed-source commercial; Community GPLv3
license_history.note: Open-core licensing blog dated 2018-11-15; Commons Clause had been added to the AGPL Enterprise terms before that.

relicensing_events.fork: PureThink's redistribution of Neo4j Enterprise with the Commons Clause removed
relicensing_events.outcome_note: Neo4j sued. The court found a DMCA violation for removing the clause and trademark infringement, and on 2024-07-22 (N.D. Cal.) awarded $597,000 in actual damages.

risk_events: 2018: Enterprise closed; Commons Clause dispute and litigation against PureThink
2024-11: Bloomberg reported preparations for a US listing; no IPO confirmed in fetched pages
robustness: Single vendor; Community Edition (GPLv3) is forkable, but Neo4j has shown it will enforce licence terms and trademarks in court. 1,700 customers and 84% of the Fortune 100 (2024); expected positive cash flow (TechCrunch, Nov 2024).
openness_effect_assessment: GPL/AGPL dual licensing built a large graph-database community, and closing Enterprise in 2018 did not stop growth: revenue doubled in three years to over $200M by 2024 and the valuation reached $2.2B. Unlike the Elastic and Redis forks, the unauthorized redistribution of Enterprise was stopped in court, showing that licence enforcement can replace market competition when no hyperscaler backs a fork.
key_takeaway: Neo4j fought a fork of its relicensed code in court rather than in the market, and won, the opposite of OpenSearch or Valkey, where hyperscaler backers made forks durable. Closing Enterprise did not dent growth: about $550M raised, a $2.2B valuation and over $200M in revenue by 2024, with IPO preparation reported.
